what: Revolution Medicines develops cancer medicines that target RAS, a protein mutated in many of the hardest cancers to treat, including most pancreatic cancer. Its lead compounds are in late-stage trials and it has no approved product yet.
customers: None yet for medicines; its future customers would be oncologists and health systems.
money: it has essentially no product revenue
moat: A chemistry approach to inhibiting RAS in its active state, an area many companies have tried and failed at for forty years, protected by patents and trial data.
risks: It has no approved product and loses close to $2 billion a year
Late-stage trials can fail, and the shares would fall very sharply if they did
It will need to raise more money or partner before any launch
Large pharmaceutical companies are working on the same target
opportunities: Pancreatic cancer has very few effective treatments, so an approval would meet a real gap
Cash of about $3.7 billion funds it for several years
Analysts see large upside, reflecting the size of the opportunity if trials succeed
watch: Late-stage trial readouts in pancreatic and lung cancer, and the cash runway.
